diagnosis.health: Healthy, and the first four worker iterations are better than I expected. 4/4 shipped, zero reverts, zero briefs rejected, evidence verdict agrees with self-verdict every time, and the diffs are substantial rather than token: 46, 88, 86, 80 source lines. No stall signal has fired. Every iteration ran its gates in anger and three of the four caught something the gates alone would have let through. The one real defect is in the harness, not the town: RUNLOG.jsonl records secs=0, costUsd=0, turns=0, tokens=null on every worker row — only the manager row carries numbers — so the exact failure the loop was built to catch (cost per iteration climbing while output stays flat) is currently unmeasurable, and stall.mjs's $0.28/iter is an artefact of averaging one manager row across five. Raised as c12 and flagged to the human; it needs run-loop.sh, not a worker brief.
diagnosis.balance: By loop-work the grid is almost flat and almost empty: river, sky, life and plaza have one iteration each; Courtyard & garden, Lane & market and Cross street & allotments have had none at all. Cross street is the longest untouched of anything (pre7). By kind it is starker — the loop has used exactly two of seven: connect x2, deepen x2. new-element, new-ca, polish, interaction and scale are all at zero for the loop, and interaction and scale are at zero for the town's entire history including the 31 hand-driven iterations. This batch touches five different domains and four different kinds on purpose.

rationale:
Rung 2 again, deliberately and for the last time at this width. The rule is that a stall forces me up the ladder; nothing here is stalling, and rungs 1-2 still have obvious unmined ground — three domains the loop has never touched and five of seven kinds unused. Climbing now would be spending the strong moves out of impatience rather than need.

The diagnosis that shapes the batch: iterations 2-5 each shipped a system and each left it with fewer readers than it deserves, and that is now the town's characteristic shape. bellUntil was written and unread (fixed at #2). cloudCover() was added at #3 and has exactly ONE reader, the rain roll — a probe measured a 27 s median lead between cover crossing 0.5 and the first drop, and the town spends every second of it behaving as though the sky were clear. updateBoat has none. So b5 and b8 are the same move applied twice, at different scales.

I checked four candidate gaps against the source before writing, per the standing watch note, and two died there. 'Nobody shelters from the rain' is wrong: umbrellas go up at line 1297, unumbrella'd walkers speed up 1.5x at 782, sitters get up at 765, and every spawn rate already scales by raining. What is actually missing is not the reaction but its *timing* — everything reacts to `raining`, a boolean that flips in a single frame, and nothing reads the half-day of warning that now exists. 'The allotments have no crop system' is also wrong: SPECIES carries four veg entries and speciesFor() splits the CA on inAllotment. What is missing there is the other half of the cycle — nothing is ever picked. Both survived as briefs, but as much smaller and more accurate ones than the versions I would have written from the cue list. I also corrected c11 outright: people do cross the bridge (the lane IS the bridge, 114 to 127 carried at y 66.4), they just never stop on it.

Ordering. b5 first because it is the frontier and the batch's real bet — it touches the largest system added so far, it has a legibility trap and a pop trap in it, and it is the one that could fail. b6 is the risk-balanced middle. b7 fixes the single largest visual pop in the town and is the safest big-payoff item. b8 and b9 are small, close three cues between them, and are there so a stale plan still has cheap useful work at the end of it rather than the batch degrading into whatever the worker invents.

Still NOT reaching for c1 (the world stops progressing after ~15 real minutes, rung 4). Second pass holding it. The condition for spending it is a batch that comes back thin, and this one has five briefs that each name a real absence I verified in the source. Nor am I briefing Courtyard & garden, which the loop has never touched — I looked, and it is the best-developed part of the town (CA ring, dieback, daisies, desire paths, sweeper, nappers, picnickers, butterflies, fireflies). Its gap is a rung-5 gap: there is no way to *read* the courtyard, only to watch it. That is the same shelf c1 sits on.

queue.brief: announce() assigns tickerEl.textContent outright (~line 534), so two events in the same frame show only the second — the town's one text surface silently drops lines and has done since it was built. That is also what blocks c4: the church-answer branch in strikeClock (~line 3143) is unreachable dead code, because `(hInt === 9 || hInt === 18)` hangs off an else-if under `(hInt % 3 === 0)` and both 9 and 18 are divisible by three; it cannot simply be un-nested while a second announce in the same frame would erase the first. Fix the cause, then the symptom: make announce() a small ordered queue with a minimum dwell per line, and then let the church actually answer the clock at nine and eighteen.
queue.successLooksLike: At nine o'clock on day 2 or later you read the clock line and then the church line, in that order, both legible; no line is ever cut off mid-word by another.
queue.avoid: Do not grow the ticker into a log or a second UI element — it is one line and should stay one line. Do not let the queue back up; drop stale entries rather than showing an old line late.
